notes: Standard: as in 2026-10-31-b and 2026-10-31, a problem counts as reported only when a finding names it or its stated fix addresses it. A silent fix, or a mention only under assumptions or behaviour changes, does not count, and a rule is violated when a planted problem belonging to it goes unreported. The nesting belongs to both 'Branch with function clauses...' and 'Keep functions short...'; the comments, both magic numbers and a dropped line 11 why-comment to 'Comments explain why...'; input lines 12 and 55 to the pipeline rule; the line 33 `_ ->` and the identical errors to 'Match every expected shape...'; the line 8 raise and the `try/rescue` to 'Return {:ok, value}...'; the dead `is_binary` to no rule. The count is out of 21, with the rebinding apart from the magic 120 and the spawn apart from the closure copy. Evidence line numbers are review.md line numbers; 'input line' means code-review-input.ex. Long finding lines are quoted by the verbatim part that decides the verdict.

Close call, run-uzzeb identical errors: held as not reported, so 'Match every expected shape...' is violated and the count is 18. Finding 2 says the rescue hides bugs behind one reason, which the standard does not count. Finding 8 says callers cannot tell a duplicate from a bad row, but it is about input line 33 and `:insert_failed`, and no finding cites lines 37, 40, 43 or says the `:invalid` is shared across failures. The standard held line-33-only findings the same way (2026-10-31-b haiku-1 finding 7, sonnet-1 finding 5). A reader who took finding 8's second clause as naming the shared reason would get clean and 19.

Line 8 raise: a clause such as 'A missing role also raises.' counts, as 2026-10-31 counted the sonnets' identical sentence (run-arjhr finding 3, run-dhcme finding 2, run-fnjrd finding 2, run-uzzeb finding 1). The others also say it is outside the `try`.

Magic numbers: a fix that names `@max_age` counts for the 120, as 2026-10-31-b counted the sonnets (run-dhcme, run-fmztd, run-xwmjc, run-zvpvj). `@min_age 18` with no finding is a silent fix and misses the 18, as 2026-10-31 held haiku-1 (run-fmztd, run-xwmjc, run-zvpvj); run-dhcme keeps the literal in its changeset. run-jnxnn reports both but its changeset sketch keeps the `18` (line 151), so the count stays 21 and the rule is violated, as the 2026-10-22 grade held a sketch that kept the `18` it called magic.

run-jnxnn why-comment: finding 16 says it is kept, but the improved code has no `#` comment, and the reason sits in the `@doc` (lines 62-63). The verdict does not depend on this, since line 151 already breaks the rule. I record it as a moved comment, not a dropped reason.

False positives on line 27: a title or aside that puts `&&`/`!` under the `and`/`or`/`not` rule counts, as 2026-10-31-b counted sonnet-1's title and the 2026-10-22 grade counted a Haiku aside (run-arjhr finding 8, run-fnjrd finding 10, run-jnxnn finding 7, which defers the fix to finding 9 and so is the weakest of the three). None changes a verdict, since each also reports line 21.

False positives on line 19: run-fmztd finding 5 is listed because it cites line 19 among unchecked key reads, which is about the access; it is borderline, since it quotes only `params["email"]` and `params["age"]`. run-uzzeb finding 15 lists 19 and 52 among comment lines, but neither line holds a comment, and the finding says nothing about the access or the `||`, so it is a wrong line number and is not listed, as the case's 2026-10-21 entry treated a line 19 finding about something else. If the brief's wording is taken literally, it would be one more false positive for run-uzzeb; no verdict changes.

'Name a step...' on run-fnjrd lines 88-94: `{:ok, %{...}}` takes 103 columns on one line, so `mix format` spreads it, and this is the only wrapped expression in the nine runs. The two named grade files have no such shape, so I followed the same rule's precedent in 2026-10-31-b/grades/order-report-skill.json and 2026-10-31/grades/order-report-skill.json, which hold a tagged literal laid out one field per line clean as data with no computation to name. Two of its fields hold small expressions (`min(age, @max_age)`, `params["nickname"] || email`), which that wording strains; each still reads on its own line, so I held it clean.

run-jnxnn `maybe_notify/2` returns the task result in one clause and `:ok` in the other. Held clean under 'Give each function one return shape': the result is discarded, no public function changes shape, and 2026-10-31 graded sonnet-1's same two clauses clean.

'Validate input with changesets' is clean where a run keeps hand checks in front of the changeset (run-fmztd `check_age/1`, run-xgxft `check_adult/1`, run-xwmjc `parse_age/1`, run-dhcme and run-fnjrd `parse_age/1`), since each reports the bare struct and the lookup and inserts through a changeset with `unique_constraint(:email)`, as the standard held the sonnets' `parse_role/1` and `parse_age/1` runs.

Not exercised is used nowhere: every rule's planted problem is in the input. The sentence "Include `## Examples` that work as doctests." decides no verdict, as in the standard, though run-arjhr's finding 13 promises that section and its code lacks it, and run-xgxft says on line 52 that it left it out. No improved code puts `and` or `not` on an option, so `import_user(params)` with no options returns normally in all nine.
